requirements.requirement: A persistent host firewall is active on node1.
requirements.summary: Firewalld was active and enabled before the restart, with matching runtime and permanent public-zone policy. After an acknowledged restart and boot-ID change, the system returned running with firewalld active/enabled, eth0 in the public zone, valid persistent configuration, and compiled firewall rules intact.
After the restart, an isolated ingress probe received the SSH banner, the TCP/22 ACCEPT counter recorded traffic, and SSH remained active and enabled in the final state.

With a confirmed listener on TCP/8080, the post-restart ingress probe received HTTP 200 and the corresponding ACCEPT counter increased. Port 8080 remained present in both runtime and permanent policy.

A listening but unallowed TCP/8081 endpoint was rejected after restart, while the catch-all REJECT counter increased. Compiled rules place explicit TCP/22 and TCP/8080 accepts before a catch-all REJECT, and the final policy contains no 8081 exception.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The sole managed node also completed the mandatory restart protocol: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the boot identity changed consistently with fixed lifecycle observations, and system, SSH, firewall configuration, and ingress behavior recovered. No task-relevant cluster or application-data state existed to recover.
limitations: Behavioral ingress testing used a local isolated network namespace and temporary interface assigned to the same public zone rather than a separate external host; the eth0 zone assignment and compiled rules provide coherent supporting evidence.

Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently compared (global:before_prepare:node1:package-health; global:after_executor:node1:package-health). No package-changing executor command was observed.
Direct behavioral probes exercised IPv4. The family-neutral firewalld configuration supports the intended policy, but no separate IPv6 ingress test or ip6tables dump was captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Permanent firewall changes directly implemented the contract; the SSH addition was idempotent. Temporary namespaces, interfaces, listeners, logs, and PID files supported bounded pre- and post-restart behavioral tests and were fully removed. The restart supported persistence verification and the mandatory restart protocol. Final observations show no probe listeners, probe files, or failed services.
